our_title: Nested dissection splits the context into a second random stream regardless of the deterministic option (ordering side)
ran: repro/PS2-G08-2/run.sh (30 fresh processes per thread count, SCOTCH_DETERMINISTIC=1, gord bump.grf and mord cube_8.msh): pristine 'gord threads=2 runs=30 differing_from_1thread_ref=30', 'threads=4 ... =30', mord 0; patched (0006) 'gord threads=1/2/4 ... differing=0', mord 0. check_prog_gord/mord rc=0 32/64-bit.
evidence: hgraph_order_nd.c:305 'if (contextThreadLaunchSplit (grafptr->contptr, (ContextSplitFunc) hgraphOrderNd2, &spltdat) != 0) /* If counld not split context to run concurrently */'; hmesh_order_nd.c:261 same for hmeshOrderNd2; common_context.c:298-299 seeds a new generator for sub-context 1; s_l.tex:7900-7904 promises identical results for any number of threads.

fix_options.label: a. Guard the two ordering callers like G12's 0009 (committed)
fix_options.summary: Include context.h, read CONTEXTOPTIONNUMDETERMINISTIC, run the two sub-tasks in sequence when set: '(deteval != 0) || (contextThreadLaunchSplit (...) != 0)'. Identical idiom and wording to kgraph_map_rb_part.c in G12's 0009; G06's alt b verified.
fix_options.tested: 30x3 determinism runs gord/mord pristine vs patched, check_prog_gord/mord 32/64-bit
fix_options.tradeoffs: Loses task-level concurrency of nested dissection under the deterministic option (each half still uses all threads internally).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Consumer-side option check with '#include "context.h"' as in graph_match.c:205-212; mirrors his contextThreadLaunchSplit fallback structure.

fix_options.label: b. Refuse to split in contextThreadLaunchSplit() when the option is set (G06's alt a)
fix_options.summary: One guard in common_context.c for all five callers.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Layering: the common layer would depend on libscotch's option numbering, and dgraphFoldDup()'s random-free split would be serialized too.

our_title: hgraphOrderCc() leaves uninitialized column block cells when a component ordering fails; orderExit() then frees garbage
ran: repro/GRA-25: pristine `./leak g dbl2.grf 'o{strat=b{cmin=0,strat=s}}'` (SCOTCH_graphOrder: compute fails, SCOTCH_graphOrderExit runs) -> 'hgraphOrderCc: cannot compute ordering on induced graph' then 'AddressSanitizer: BUS on unknown address (pc ... bp 0xbebebebebebebeae ...) ... #3 free' from orderExit2; patched (0004): 'order ret=1', clean. Also triggered through hgraphOrderCp() + 0003.
evidence: hgraph_order_cc.c:173 'cblkptr->cblknbr = rootnbr;' then :177-184 initializes cblktab[rootnum] inside the per-component loop, :197-200 'if (o != 0) { errorPrint (...); break; }' leaves cells rootnum+1.. uninitialized; order.c:145-149 orderExit2 frees cblktab[cblknum].cblktab for all cblknbr cells.

fix_options.label: a. Initialize all cells before ordering any component (committed)
fix_options.summary: Move the cell initialization loop before the ordering loop, as hgraphOrderNd() does for its three cells.
fix_options.tested: repro/GRA-25 third case 32-bit; check_prog_gord (disconnected.grf with -cd), 64-bit checks
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Same construction order as his hgraphOrderNd() (hgraph_order_nd.c:228-236).

fix_options.label: b. Free the partial tree on error
fix_options.summary: memFree cblktab and reset cblknbr on the error path.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Sub-trees of already ordered components would leak unless recursively freed.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Leaves the tree inconsistent for the Order destructor.

our_title: hgraphOrderBl()/hmeshOrderBl() re-run their strategy on every sub-block: no termination for tree-building strategies
ran: repro/GRA-22: `timeout 10 ./bl 'b{cmin=100,strat=n{sep=m{vert=50,low=h{pass=10},asc=f{move=100}},ole=s,ose=s}}' 100 0` pristine rc=124; patched 207 blocks, SCOTCH_graphOrderCheck=0. `timeout 10 mord dbl.msh /dev/null '-ob{cmin=2,strat=n{sep=h,ole=s,ose=s}}'` pristine rc=124, patched rc=0.
evidence: hgraph_order_bl.c:192 'if (hgraphOrderBl (grafptr, ordeptr, ordenum, cblkptr->cblktab + cblknum, paraptr) != 0)' -> :96 'hgraphOrderSt (grafptr, ordeptr, ordenum, cblkptr, paraptr->straptr)' on the whole graph again; s_l.tex:1357-1360 says the tree is traversed 'without changing the ordering that has been computed'.

fix_options.label: a. Separate strategy run from leaf splitting (committed with GRA-22)
fix_options.summary: Static hgraphOrderBl2()/hmeshOrderBl2() walk the tree with the ordering offset of each sub-block.

fix_options.label: b. Minimal: forbid tree-building strategies inside 'b'
fix_options.summary: Return an error when the strategy produced a tree (cblktab != NULL after hgraphOrderSt).

our_title: Weighted block splitting leaves trailing zero-load columns out of every block
ran: repro/GRA-22: `./bl 'b{cmin=1,strat=s}' 1 2` (loads 1 1 1 1 1 1 0 0): pristine 'covered=6/8 rang_end=6', SCOTCH_graphOrderCheck=1 ('orderCheck2: invalid number of vertex nodes (2)'); patched 'covered=8/8' check=0; also cmin=2.
evidence: hgraph_order_bl.c:172 '} while (vnlosum < grafptr->vnlosum); /* As long as columns remain */' stops when the load sum is reached although zero-load columns (graphCheck allows velotax >= 0, graph_check.c:177) remain.

fix_options.label: a. Last block absorbs remaining zero-weight columns; loop on columns (committed with GRA-22)
b. Reject zero vertex loads in 'b'
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He accepts zero loads everywhere else.

our_title: Shrinking memRealloc() of the coarse edge array is unchecked: NULL edge array on failure (tree-wide pattern)
ran: repro/GRA-14 with the patched library: N=9 (1 thread) / N=23 (4 threads): 'graph_check.c:138:15: runtime error: load of null pointer' then SEGV in graphCheck after SCOTCH_graphCoarsen returned 0 with edgetax == NULL - baseval.
read_only: Other instances only read: bgraph_bipart_bd.c:430, dgraph_induce.c:239/244, dmesh_dgraph.c:645, hgraph_order_cp.c:433, dgraph_coarsen.c:1269/1271, dgraph_redist.c:475.
evidence: graph_coarsen.c:470-471 'coaredgetab = memRealloc (coargrafptr->edgetax + baseval, ...); coargrafptr->edgetax = (Gnum *) coaredgetab - baseval;'.

fix_options.label: a. Keep the larger array when the shrink fails
fix_options.summary: Test the memRealloc() result; on NULL keep the old block (still valid after a failed realloc).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Would have to be applied to ~8 sites to be coherent; shrinking reallocs do not fail with glibc.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: The tree deliberately leaves shrinking reallocs unchecked; a global decision for the maintainer, not a one-site patch.

fix_options.label: b. Leave as is (status quo)
fix_options.summary: Document that shrinking reallocs are assumed not to fail.

our_title: Manual says ordering lines may appear in any order; orderLoad() rejects unsorted lines
ran: repro/GRA-03: `gotst p4.grf shuffled.ord /dev/null` -> 'orderLoad: bad input (3)' (pristine and patched).
evidence: s_f.tex:756 'Ordering pairs can be stored in any order in the file; however, indices of source vertices must be all different.' vs order_io.c:112 'if (vertval != (vertnum + ordeptr->baseval)) { errorPrint ("orderLoad: bad input (3)");'.

fix_options.label: a. Fix the manual (doc/ is G28's)
fix_options.summary: State that lines must be in increasing vertex order.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He documents the loader as it is; mapLoad accepts any order because it sorts labels, orderLoad never did.

fix_options.label: b. Make the loader accept any order
fix_options.summary: Index on the vertex index read, add a final completeness pass.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Larger change for no known user.
